name: MCP Server Scaffold
blurb: an MCP server skeleton in Python or TypeScript from the tools, resources and prompts you describe
intro: Writes an MCP server skeleton from the tools (with typed, described parameters and annotations), resources (URIs and URI templates) and prompts you define: Python on the official mcp SDK (2.x MCPServer or 1.x FastMCP) or TypeScript on @modelcontextprotocol/sdk (McpServer with zod schemas), over stdio or Streamable HTTP, with package files, a README and the Claude Code and Claude Desktop config. It lints what the model will read: names, missing descriptions, and state-changing tools not marked destructive.

inputs.label: Server name
inputs.help: Lower case, - or _; becomes the config key.

inputs.label: Server description
inputs.default: Drives the lab bench: serial console, power supply and SWD probe of the device under test.

default.name: read_serial
default.description: Read text from a serial port for a number of seconds and return it. Use it to capture the boot log of the device under test.

default.name: set_psu_voltage
default.description: Set the output voltage of one bench power supply channel. The output stays enabled.

default.name: erase_flash
default.description: Erase the target's flash through the SWD probe.

inputs.label: Tool parameters

default.name: seconds
default.description: How long to listen, in seconds

default.name: mass_erase
default.description: Erase every sector, not only the application region

inputs.help: One row per parameter; Values = enum values (comma-separated) or the default of an optional one.

inputs.label: Resources

default.name: instruments
default.description: Instruments on the bench with their VISA addresses

default.name: run_log
default.description: Serial log of one test run

inputs.help: URI or URI template with {name} variables.

inputs.label: Prompts

default.name: triage_uart_log
default.description: Explain a boot log and suggest the next measurement

inputs.help: Args comma-separated, ? = optional; use {arg} in the text.

input.description: Searches the team's engineering docs and returns matching sections with their source links.

tools.description: Full-text search over the engineering docs. Returns up to `limit` sections with title, path and a snippet.

prompts.description: Summarize a docs page for a design review

usage: Give name, description, language (python|typescript), py_sdk (v2|v1), transport (stdio|http) and port, and tables: tools {name, description, annotation none|read-only|destructive|idempotent|open-world}, params {tool, name, type string|integer|number|boolean|enum|string[]|number[], required yes|no, description, values = enum list or default}, resources {uri, name, description, mime}, prompts {name, description, args 'a, b?', text with {a}}. It returns the source file, package files, README.md, 'Client config' (.mcp.json, claude mcp add, Claude Desktop) and a lint table. SDK versions are as of 2026-09; check before pinning.
